name: soxhlet-siphon-cycle
title: Soxhlet Siphon Cycle
description: A card-scale status widget modelled on a Soxhlet extractor's siphon cycle: an extraction chamber fills drop by drop over 19.8s until the liquid crosses the siphon arm's overflow height, then self-primes and drains almost instantly back into the boiling flask below in 0.6s, before the fill begins again — a loading indicator whose whole identity is the slow-fill/fast-dump asymmetry.
useWhen: a loading/progress indicator standing in for a generic spinner on a long-running background process, where the process is well represented by a single value building slowly toward a hard threshold and then discharging almost instantly. Reach for autoclave-cycle-gauge instead when the process has three distinct phases (ramp, hold, fast release) told apart by needle speed rather than a single fill-then-dump threshold event; reach for progress-wick or progress-hatch instead for a plain monotonic completion fraction with no discharge/reset cycle.
instruction: Build <SoxhletSiphonCycle label? className?> as a self-contained 2D canvas widget inside a bordered card (rounded-md border border-border bg-surface, fixed 4:5 canvas aspect-ratio, geometry derived entirely from the container's smaller dimension via min(width, height) so the apparatus rescales cleanly at card size). It renders, top to bottom, a condenser drip line, an extraction chamber (rect outline, height = 0.4 * min-dimension), a siphon-threshold tick mark near the chamber's top-right, a 4-point siphon tube polyline running from the chamber's mouth down into a round flask below. CYCLE: three phases driven by elapsed real time via a fixed-step rAF loop — a fill phase where one condensate drop falls from the drip line every 900ms, each drop raising the chamber liquid level by 100/22 percent (22 drops = 19.8s, 0% to 100%, matching the spec's headline 19.8s/22-drop anchor exactly; the spec's separately-stated 2.5%-per-drop figure only sums to 55% over 22 drops and cannot itself reach the stated 100% trigger, so it is treated as the spec's own rounding slip and the 22-drops/100%/19.8s statement is taken as authoritative), a dump phase once level reaches 100% where the chamber self-primes and drains over a fast 600ms, and a 400ms settle pause at empty before the next drop begins. The dump is rendered as a value-only bottom-to-top wipe: an opacity boundary rises from the chamber floor to the pre-dump liquid surface over the 600ms, clearing what has already drained and leaving what has not yet, with a soft leading edge at the wipe boundary so it reads as a sweep rather than a blink — never a level-height jump and never a colour-based cue. A synced flow highlight travels the siphon tube polyline from chamber mouth to flask over the same 600ms. The instant the drain completes, the flask's own liquid line (rendered inside a clipped circle, density rising with accumulated volume rather than hue) ticks up a fixed 4% of its cap; the accumulation is capped and reset every 5 completed cycles (~100s) so the loop stays unbounded. A falling drop between the drip line and the current liquid surface is drawn with a quadratic ease-in during the first 480ms of each 900ms drop interval. TOKENS: every stroke/fill reads var(--foreground) or var(--border) exclusively, resolved once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) with zero literal fallback of any kind; the mount routine retries on the next rAF until both tokens resolve and paints nothing before that; re-reads on every documentElement class-attribute mutation via a MutationObserver, and a ResizeObserver keeps canvas pixel dimensions and DPR in sync. --border is used strictly as a non-load-bearing glass-rim outline (chamber, tube, flask, drip line, threshold tick) and is never a fill; chamber and flask liquid fills are var(--foreground) at moderate, level-dependent alpha. No --ns-accent anywhere — this is a resting, non-interactive status surface, not a control. REDUCED MOTION: freezes at the 85%-full frame — liquid level near the siphon arm's mouth, clearly about to cross the threshold, the single most structured, tension-loaded frame — rendered once, synchronously, with no rAF loop, no timers, and no observers driving motion. An IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop when the card scrolls off-screen and re-arms it (re-checking tokens for a theme flip that happened while hidden) on re-entry. Cleanup on unmount cancels every pending rAF and disconnects all three observers. No pointer interaction — the one followable thing is the liquid level in the chamber, rising steadily for ~20s and then vanishing in under a second; nothing else needs separate animation to make the mechanic read.
